done_when: When forge merge merges a story's last task, it writes the story's done record in that same merge, from an outcome given with --outcome or taken from the story's title, and forge story done is only needed to change that outcome later; no separate pull request. New and existing repos: same in any repo on this release; stories already marked done are untouched. One command-level test: merging the last task leaves the story done with no extra pull request.

findings.body: The earlier concurrency gap remains open. Two independent final tasks can both evaluate this predicate before either merge reaches their fetched origin/default snapshot, so neither includes the completion marker. The fetch in src/forge/repo.py:174 precedes checks.wait, and there is no refresh or coordination before this decision. Both PRs can then merge successfully, but story.completed (src/forge/story.py:630–643) finds no marker and leaves the story unfinished. This also affects forge land through src/forge/land.py:81. Coordinate sibling merges and refresh their landed state before deciding which merge records completion.
findings.title: Preserve completion when sibling tasks merge concurrently

why: Recording that a story is done opens a separate fix and pull request just to write one record, costing a full review and CI run per story
